co_secret_crag_aka_ridge_6.blurb: A small, quiet crag high on the southeast side of Eldorado Mountain above Boulder, with sixteen routes, most of them bolted and a few trad lines. Climbs are mostly 70 to 100 feet, and a 60 m rope helps on the longer ones. Grades start around 5.6 but the bulk sit in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a handful of 5.12s on top, so it suits climbers comfortable on harder sport. The sandstone is solid and the wall faces south, which keeps it warm. Routes are laid out in tiers and numbered from the west end. The base is a steep slab reached by a scramble, and the crag sees few visitors compared with the rest of the mountain.

co_upper_east_face_2.blurb: Up a gully on the right flank of East Blob Rock sits this steep face, at about 7,100 feet in Boulder Canyon. About sixteen routes mix gear-protected and bolted lines, with trad making up most of them. Grades run from 5.8 into the 5.13s, centred on 5.10 to 5.12, so there is a little for moderate climbers and plenty for strong ones. It holds the canyon's best-known multi-pitch sport line alongside steeper single-pitch test pieces. You reach it by taking the Blob Rock trail, dropping right beneath the slab, and scrambling up the gully, so expect a short but steep approach.

co_slamdance_buttress.blurb: A short buttress on Lily Mountain, just south of Estes Park and set slightly off the hiking trail. Sixteen routes, mostly bolted sport with a couple of trad lines, stand about 25 to 40 feet tall. Grades are friendly: most fall between 5.8 and 5.10, with a few easier lines and one or two harder ones, making it a good stop for newer leaders and families. The west face has odd, wavy rock with pockets and bulges, though the bases of some routes are crumbly enough to want a spotter. The approach is a mostly level walk of around three-quarters of a mile.

co_upper_animal_world.blurb: The uppermost cliff of Animal World in Boulder Canyon, perched above the highway and known as a magnet for 5.12 sport climbers. Around sixteen routes, mostly bolted and a few trad, are steep and well protected, with a spread from a single 5.10 through plenty of 5.11 and 5.12 to several 5.13s. A few lines are two pitches or need a long rappel, but most are single pitch. The east-facing wall catches the morning and goes into shade later in the day. Rockfall is a real worry because the highway sits below, so move carefully around loose stones.

co_woodstone.blurb: A compact sport crag in the Estes Park Valley near Lily Lake, one of three close neighbours that share a small alcove used for gearing up. Nearly all of its sixteen routes are bolted, with a single trad line, and many are recent additions. Grades span from the 5.6 range up to 5.13, but the weight is on 5.11 with a few harder tests, so it favours strong climbers. Reaching it takes a half-hour or so of walking through woods and talus. At close to 10,000 feet the setting is high and open, with views of the peaks and valley from the alcove.
